summary: 25 blocking findings. Three reference findings were real (the binary-buffer newline state, twice, and recursion in the matcher); two more were true of our errata rather than of the program, and one named a program behaviour the errata lacked; one is refuted by execution. Eighteen verifier findings: seventeen coverage gaps answered with cases the panel can read, one overstrict static audit removed.

findings.summary: Reading a newline-terminated file after a binary buffer with an unterminated final line incorrectly transfers the old line's missing-newline flag to the newly read final line.
findings.rationale: Right, and mine: the reference kept a per-line missing-newline flag and moved it onto the newly read last line. GNU ed (io.c) keeps one remembered line node, set when a read at the end of a binary buffer ends without a newline or reads nothing, and leaves the newline off only while that node is still the last line; the reference now keeps that node and its message and byte-count rules, errata entry 21 states the behaviour, and 58 binary-state scripts taken from the program at run time pin it.

gate.rule: wrong path unterminated-never-remembered: a reference that never remembers the unterminated line must fail test_odd_files; errata-map entry 21 pins the states with graded cases

findings.summary: Reading a newline-terminated file after a binary buffer with an unterminated last line incorrectly removes the newline from the newly appended last line.
findings.rationale: Right, and mine: the reference kept a per-line missing-newline flag and moved it onto the newly read last line. GNU ed (io.c) keeps one remembered line node, set when a read at the end of a binary buffer ends without a newline or reads nothing, and leaves the newline off only while that node is still the last line; the reference now keeps that node and its message and byte-count rules, errata entry 21 states the behaviour, and 58 binary-state scripts taken from the program at run time pin it.

gate.rule: wrong path unterminated-never-remembered; errata-map entry 21

findings.summary: A backslash-continued global list stops consuming input at its empty continuation line, so a following q executes after all selected lines instead of as part of the list.
findings.rationale: The program and the reference agree (each selected line printed twice, then the q runs), so the reference is right; the defect was ours all the same, in the errata: entry 16 said a following q is taken as part of the list, which is false, and the panel graded the reference against that sentence. The entry (now 18) says the empty line does not end with a backslash, so the line after it is the next command, and two graded cases hold the q and a ,n in that position.

gate.rule: errata-map: every errata entry names graded cases whose expected result comes from the program, checked by check_coverage_map.py; an entry may state only what a graded case shows

findings.summary: Valid long bounded-repeat regular expressions are parsed but matched by unbounded Python recursion, causing an unhandled RecursionError instead of GNU ed's successful substitution.
findings.rationale: Right, and mine: the matcher enumerated matches through a chain of generators, one frame per repetition, so a 2,000-character line overflowed the recursion limit and a star over a long line was quadratic. posixre now compiles the expression to a small program and walks it depth-first in pattern order, exploring each (instruction, position) once per search, with a bounded run of one character class as a single instruction; 126,000 random searches agree with the old matcher and long-line scripts run in well under a second. Probing the boundary also found that GNU ed refuses a repeat count above 32767, now errata entry 11.

gate.rule: regex cases over the 4,000- and 70,000-byte fixtures (bounded repeats, stars, nested stars, a count of 32767 and 32768) in tests/cases/regex.jsonl; coverage-map finding 4

findings.summary: The append command accepts a reversed two-address range, although only '=' may accept one under the GNU ed 1.19 erratum.
findings.rationale: GNU ed accepts 2,1a and inserts after line 1, as the manual's rule for a one-address command says (the last address is used), and the reference does the same; the panel read errata entry 3, which wrongly said every command but = rejects a reversed pair. The entry now states the rule for one-address and range commands and is pinned by graded cases for a, i, k, c, d, j, s, g and more.

gate.rule: errata-map entry 3; wrong path reversed-range-rejected-for-a must fail test_append_insert_change

findings.summary: The append command clears the undo stack before determining whether input mode inserts any line, so a successful empty append wrongly destroys the prior undoable buffer modification.
findings.rationale: GNU ed clears the undo stack when a or i reads no line, and the reference does too, so the reference is right; but the manual does not say so and the errata did not either, which is what the panel read. Errata entry 14 now states it, with graded cases for a, i and c.

gate.rule: errata-map entry 14; wrong path empty-append-keeps-undo must fail test_append_insert_change

findings.summary: The substitution parser accepts a repeat-form suffix character such as g as an explicit substitution delimiter, although the contract excludes characters used by the alternate repeat-substitution syntax.
findings.rationale: Refuted by execution: on the finding's own script sgxgyg GNU ed 1.19 prints ? and leaves the line as x, and so does the returned reference, because the repeat form is parsed first and g, p, r and digits are never taken as delimiters; l, n and a are accepted as delimiters by both. The scripts are now graded cases so the point stays pinned. Rows F7 and F7b to F7i of that receipt hold the scripts.

gate.rule: coverage-map finding 7: the delimiter scripts are graded cases

contract_citation.anchor: where the manual and the program disagree the program is what counts

findings.contested_in_channel: prepared in revision-v5/contest-note.md for #terminus-3-submissions; this environment cannot post to the channel, so the note must be posted by hand before the resubmission is judged

findings.summary: Fixture construction cannot create an existing subdirectory, so the verifier cannot distinguish an ed implementation that rejects otherwise valid file-command paths beneath one.
findings.rationale: Right: the returned workdir opened each fixture name directly and never made a directory, so no case could put a file under one. A fixture name with a directory part now creates it, a name ending in a slash is a directory alone, the comparison walks the whole tree, and seven cases write, read and load files under sub/, with and without -r.

gate.rule: coverage-map finding 8; verifier fixture names may hold a directory part and the snapshot walks the tree

findings.summary: No shown case checks that '&' repeats an entire multiline G or V command list rather than just its first command.
findings.rationale: The returned corpus held no case for this behaviour (returned-no-such-case.json), and GNU ed and the reference agree on the finding's script, so it is a coverage gap. A case is added (a G list of two lines repeated by &) in the family file the panel reads, with its expected result taken from GNU ed 1.19 at run time; the four case files the panel reported NOT SHOWN were under the per-file limit, so the whole corpus is now held under the panel's total read budget as well.

findings.summary: The reference never enforces GNU ed's documented maximum line length or maximum number of lines, instead storing lines and counts in unbounded Python objects.
findings.rationale: The instruction bounded the number of lines but not their length, so a two-gigabyte line was inside the domain. The instruction now says no line is longer than a hundred thousand bytes, which keeps the 70,000-byte fixture and puts INT_MAX outside the domain; the reference handles lines of that length in well under a second.

gate.rule: instruction: every input dimension the verifier can vary carries a stated bound (lines per file, bytes per line)

findings.summary: The package audit mistakes an executable-format magic prefix in inert data for a delivered executable program, falsely rejecting a contract-legal submission.
findings.rationale: Right: the static package audit rejected any delivered file whose first bytes look like an executable, a rule the instruction never stated (it says the three construction rules are checked while the program runs). The audit and its self-test are removed; the launcher, which stops a process start, native code and a foreign import at run time, remains the enforcer with its six probe programs.

gate.rule: restriction X-stdlib-no-programs is enforced only by the run-time launcher named in the instruction; a static check the instruction does not announce is not added again
